name: URL change watcher
description: Poll a URL on a schedule and notify only when its content changes. Zero AI verbs, so it costs zero tokens per fire; remembers the last digest and a failure streak in workflow state.
notes: The canonical zero-LLM scheduled job. Fire it with a recurring TODO bound to this tool (workflow_id=url_watcher, workflow_params={url, alert_after_failures}). PREREQUISITE: fetch_url_nymeria is an opt-in catalog tool and must be enabled on the thread the TODO runs in, or the watcher reports an unrecoverable fetch failure. State is keyed per url (workflow state is namespaced only by workflow_id + user_id, and one installed tool serves every TODO), so one tool can watch many URLs. Detects fetch failure by the tool's '[Error]:' return (fetch_url_nymeria never raises), and uses a stable hashlib digest (not the per-process hash()) so a fresh subprocess compares correctly across fires. Point it at a STABLE url (a redirect to a varying URL flaps the digest). See docs/agent-systems/triggers.md and the cookbook.

import hashlib


def state_key(prefix: str, url: str) -> str:
    """A PER-URL state key, because state is not namespaced by parameter.

    Workflow state is namespaced by (workflow_id, user_id) only, and this recipe
    installs as ONE global tool, so every TODO bound to it shares a single state
    document. Without the url folded into the key, two watched URLs would
    overwrite each other's digest and report a change on every fire, forever.
    """
    return f"{prefix}:{hashlib.sha256(url.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:16]}"


def run(url: str, alert_after_failures: int = 3):
    """Poll a URL and notify only when its content changes. Zero AI, zero tokens.

    Remembers the last content digest and a consecutive-failure streak in this
    workflow's own persistent state, keyed per url, so a transient blip never
    pages but a real change (or a sustained outage) does. Fire it on a recurring
    TODO bound to this tool (workflow_id + workflow_params) for a scheduled,
    zero-token watcher.

    Requires the fetch_url_nymeria tool to be ENABLED ON THE THREAD the TODO
    runs in: it is an opt-in catalog tool, not a default one, and a workflow
    resolves tools against its thread. Without it the watcher reports a fetch
    failure it can never recover from.

    fetch_url_nymeria signals failure by RETURNING an "[Error]: ..." string, not
    by raising, so failure is detected on the return value (a try/except is kept
    as a secondary guard). The digest covers the fetched content, which includes
    the resolved source URL line, so point this at a STABLE url: a redirect to a
    per-request-varying URL would flap the digest and page every fire.

    Args:
        url: The URL to poll.
        alert_after_failures: Notify after this many consecutive fetch failures.
    """
    alert_after_failures = max(1, alert_after_failures)
    digest_key = state_key("last_digest", url)
    failures_key = state_key("consecutive_failures", url)
    try:
        page = nym.tools.fetch_url_nymeria(url=url)
        failed = isinstance(page, str) and page.startswith("[Error]")
        detail = page if failed else ""
    except Exception as exc:
        failed, detail = True, str(exc)

    if failed:
        fails = (nym.state.get(failures_key) or 0) + 1
        nym.state.set(failures_key, fails)
        if fails == alert_after_failures:
            nym.notify(f"Watcher cannot reach {url} ({fails} tries): {detail}")
        return {"checked": False, "failures": fails}

    nym.state.set(failures_key, 0)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(str(page).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    previous = nym.state.get(digest_key)
    nym.state.set(digest_key, digest)
    if previous is None or previous == digest:
        return {"changed": False}

    nym.notify(f"{url} changed since the last check.")
    return {"changed": True}
